RI-2026-HB7183.s: Would create a program to track and report energy and water use for large buildings in Rhode Island, and set an energy performance standard for those buildings. It would affect owners and operators of large buildings. The bill was passed by both chambers and then vetoed by the Governor.
RI-2026-HB7183.src: Rhode Island legislature, summary (via Open States)

RI-2026-HB7298.s: The measure lets the town of Tiverton use different tax rates for different kinds of property. It passed and became law without the governor's signature.
RI-2026-HB7298.src: Rhode Island legislature, summary (via Open States)

RI-2026-HB7332.s: Requires public utilities to keep a customer service office in Rhode Island. The office would handle customer questions and accept bill payments. The measure became effective without the governor's signature on June 24, 2026.
RI-2026-HB7332.src: Rhode Island legislature, summary (via Open States)

RI-2026-HB7606.s: The bill sets limits on contract terms for libraries that license e-books and digital audiobooks. It would keep libraries from being held to unfair sales practices in those deals. It became law without the governor's signature on June 24, 2026.
RI-2026-HB7606.src: Rhode Island legislature, summary (via Open States)

RI-2026-HB7638.s: The law changes the rules on pedestrian right-of-way by pointing to the state list of traffic violations used when road offenses are decided. It affects drivers, pedestrians, and others who are involved in traffic cases under Rhode Island law.
RI-2026-HB7638.src: Rhode Island legislature, summary (via Open States)

RI-2026-HB7642.s: The law changes how filing fees are set for appeals from some cases decided in district court. It affects people who appeal those court decisions and became effective without the governor's signature.
RI-2026-HB7642.src: Rhode Island legislature, summary (via Open States)

RI-2026-HB7643.s: The measure changes how filing fees are figured for appeals in small claims and consumer cases decided by district court. It applies to people who appeal those cases and took effect on June 24, 2026.
RI-2026-HB7643.src: Rhode Island legislature, summary (via Open States)

RI-2026-HB7763.s: The measure would repeal some state rules on how private easements and rights-of-way are maintained. It affects people who use or own these shared access paths, and it became law without the governor's signature on June 24, 2026.
RI-2026-HB7763.src: Rhode Island legislature, summary (via Open States)

RI-2026-HB7865.s: Rhode Island’s insurance department would get a way to apply for grants to help pay for a home hardening program. Home hardening means making houses stronger against weather damage. The bill was signed by the governor.
RI-2026-HB7865.src: Rhode Island legislature, summary (via Open States)

RI-2026-HB7866.s: The bill would raise the threshold for declaring a vehicle a total loss from 80% to 85%. It affects insurance claims for damaged vehicles in Rhode Island.
RI-2026-HB7866.src: Rhode Island legislature, summary (via Open States)

RI-2026-HB7879.s: The act would direct a study of thermal energy technology to see whether thermal energy networks could meet certain goals in Rhode Island. It affects the state’s review of this kind of energy system. It became effective without the governor’s signature.
RI-2026-HB7879.src: Rhode Island legislature, summary (via Open States)

RI-2026-HB7989.s: Certain vehicles that were not made with a front plate bracket would be allowed to skip the front license plate requirement. It would apply to motor vehicles that cannot be fitted with the proper front bracket from the factory.
RI-2026-HB7989.src: Rhode Island legislature, summary (via Open States)

RI-2026-HB8104.s: Limits mortgage prepayment rules to mortgages on owner-occupied homes with one to four dwelling units. It passed both chambers and became law on June 26, 2026.
RI-2026-HB8104.src: Rhode Island legislature, summary (via Open States)

RI-2026-HB8128.s: The bill updates Rhode Island’s public accountancy law to match the 9th edition of the Uniform Accountancy Act, a model set of rules for accountants. It affects public accountants in the state. It passed both chambers and was signed by the governor on June 23, 2026.
RI-2026-HB8128.src: Rhode Island legislature, summary (via Open States)

RI-2026-HB8232.s: Changes the date of the Foster-Glocester regional school district financial meeting to March 24, 2026. It affects the Foster and Glocester school district and became effective without the governor's signature.
RI-2026-HB8232.src: Rhode Island legislature, summary (via Open States)

RI-2026-HB8348.s: The bill exempts the property of the nonprofit Mount St. Rita Health Centre in Cumberland, Rhode Island, from property tax. The exemption would take effect on December 31, 2025.
RI-2026-HB8348.src: Rhode Island legislature, summary (via Open States)

RI-2026-HB8436.s: The act changes the property tax exemption rules for elderly and disabled people in Glocester. It affects residents there who may qualify for that tax break. It took effect without the governor’s signature.
RI-2026-HB8436.src: Rhode Island legislature, summary (via Open States)

RI-2026-HB8484.s: The bill exempts Amos House’s real estate and other physical property from taxes, as long as it stays a tax-exempt nonprofit under federal law. It affects Amos House and applies to its real and tangible personal property. It became effective without the governor’s signature on June 26, 2026.
RI-2026-HB8484.src: Rhode Island legislature, summary (via Open States)

RI-2026-HB8506.s: The bill would change the pension plan terms in the labor contracts for Central Falls workers covered by that plan. It affects the city of Central Falls and the labor groups that represent those workers. It became law without the governor's signature.
RI-2026-HB8506.src: Rhode Island legislature, summary (via Open States)

RI-2026-HB8546.s: The act changes a Rhode Island law about when officers are elected at Scituate’s annual financial town meeting. It affects the town of Scituate and the timing of that election. It took effect without the governor’s signature on June 24, 2026.
RI-2026-HB8546.src: Rhode Island legislature, summary (via Open States)

RI-2026-HB8547.s: Creates a separate domestic violence calendar in Superior Court to handle felony domestic violence cases. It applies to court handling of these cases in Rhode Island and was signed by the governor.
RI-2026-HB8547.src: Rhode Island legislature, summary (via Open States)

RI-2026-HB8580.s: The measure would change the North Tiverton fire district law and cut the number of tax assessors from six to four after the annual 2026 meeting, after any voluntary resignations. It affects the district’s tax assessors. It became effective on June 26, 2026.
RI-2026-HB8580.src: Rhode Island legislature, summary (via Open States)

RI-2026-HB8590.s: The bill lets Pawtucket issue up to $5 million in bonds and notes to pay for work on public buildings. It covers building construction, repairs, upgrades, furnishing, and equipment for the city’s capital improvement program for fiscal years 2028 and 2029.
RI-2026-HB8590.src: Rhode Island legislature, summary (via Open States)

RI-2026-HB8592.s: The act allows Pawtucket to issue up to $2 million in bonds and notes to pay for street and sidewalk work. It covers design, building, rebuilding, repairs, and equipment for those roads, plus related transportation improvements like drainage and landscaping. The measure was passed by the legislature and signed by the governor.
RI-2026-HB8592.src: Rhode Island legislature, summary (via Open States)

RI-2026-HB8593.s: This act authorizes the city of Pawtucket to issue up to $2,500,000 in bonds and notes. The money would be used to improve and replace road safety infrastructure and traffic control devices in the city. The question of approving the act must be submitted to the city’s electors at the next general election, or an earlier special election if one is called.

RI-2026-HB8594.s: This act lets Pawtucket borrow up to $3 million through bonds and notes to repave streets in the city. It applies to the city’s street repaving plan for fiscal years 2028 and 2029, and it was signed by the governor.
RI-2026-HB8594.src: Rhode Island legislature, summary (via Open States)

RI-2026-HB8620.s: The act lets the city of Cranston issue up to $4 million in bonds and short-term notes to repair, build, and fix storm drains and other drainage work. It also covers work to reduce drainage and flooding problems in the city.
RI-2026-HB8620.src: Rhode Island legislature, summary (via Open States)

RI-2026-HB8621.s: The measure lets Cranston borrow up to $2,000,000 through bonds and temporary notes to buy, tear down, build, fix, change, furnish, and equip public buildings in the city. It affects the city and its public buildings. It passed and became law without the governor’s signature on June 26, 2026.
RI-2026-HB8621.src: Rhode Island legislature, summary (via Open States)

RI-2026-HB8622.s: Allows the city of Cranston to borrow up to $4 million through bonds or short-term notes to buy, build, improve, fix, or change playgrounds, sports fields, and related equipment. The money would be used in the city. It passed the legislature and became law without the governor’s signature.
RI-2026-HB8622.src: Rhode Island legislature, summary (via Open States)

RI-2026-HB8623.s: Allows the city of Cranston to borrow up to $8 million through bonds and short-term notes to design, build, repair, and improve streets, sidewalks, and bridges. The work can include paving, drainage, traffic signals, road equipment, safety upgrades, and landscaping. It became effective without the governor’s signature on June 26, 2026.
RI-2026-HB8623.src: Rhode Island legislature, summary (via Open States)

RI-2026-HB8624.s: The law lets the city of Cranston issue up to $8 million in bonds and short-term notes. The money is for fire and public safety equipment, including buying, improving, renovating, and repairing it. It became effective without the governor’s signature.
RI-2026-HB8624.src: Rhode Island legislature, summary (via Open States)

RI-2026-HB8625.s: The measure lets Cranston issue up to $25 million in bonds, notes, and other debt to pay for schools and school facilities across the city. The money could be used to buy land or buildings and to build, fix, improve, furnish, and equip school property. It became effective without the governor’s signature on June 26, 2026.
RI-2026-HB8625.src: Rhode Island legislature, summary (via Open States)

RI-2026-HB8627.s: The act lets Meghan Elizabeth McEntee officiate the marriage of Taylor Lauren Criscuolo and Michael Joseph McEntee Jr. on or about September 25, 2026, in Narragansett, Rhode Island. It applies to those named people only. It became effective without the governor’s signature.
RI-2026-HB8627.src: Rhode Island legislature, summary (via Open States)

RI-2026-HR7031.s: Creates a 15-member joint commission to study safe staffing ratios in hospitals and make recommendations. The commission would report back to the General Assembly by September 1, 2027, and end on January 30, 2028. It became effective without the governor’s signature.
RI-2026-HR7031.src: Rhode Island legislature, summary (via Open States)

RI-2026-SB2036.s: The bill exempts Blithewold, Inc.'s real estate and personal property at 101 Ferry Road in Bristol from property tax. The change applies retroactively to December 31, 2025.
RI-2026-SB2036.src: Rhode Island legislature, summary (via Open States)

RI-2026-SB2073.s: The act exempts the real and tangible personal property of Community MusicWorks in Providence from property tax. It affects that organization’s buildings and other physical property in the city. It became effective without the governor’s signature.
RI-2026-SB2073.src: Rhode Island legislature, summary (via Open States)

RI-2026-SB2260.s: The bill would set up a program for large buildings in Rhode Island to track and report energy and water use. It would also set a standard for how well those buildings use energy. The measure passed both chambers but was later vetoed by the governor.
RI-2026-SB2260.src: Rhode Island legislature, summary (via Open States)

RI-2026-SB2429.s: Public utilities would have to keep a customer service office in Rhode Island. The office would handle customer questions and take bill payments. The measure passed and became law without the governor's signature.
RI-2026-SB2429.src: Rhode Island legislature, summary (via Open States)

RI-2026-SB2475.s: Changes the rules on who must maintain private easements and rights-of-way by repealing some parts of the current law. It became law without the governor's signature.
RI-2026-SB2475.src: Rhode Island legislature, summary (via Open States)

RI-2026-SB2974.s: The law changes the state rules on pedestrian right-of-way to point to the list of traffic offense penalties in state law. It affects drivers and pedestrians by tying these violations to that penalty schedule.
RI-2026-SB2974.src: Rhode Island legislature, summary (via Open States)

RI-2026-SB2975.s: The act would make the filing fee rules simpler for people appealing small claims and consumer cases from district court. It passed the House and Senate and became effective without the governor’s signature on June 24, 2026.
RI-2026-SB2975.src: Rhode Island legislature, summary (via Open States)

RI-2026-SB3080.s: Creates a study of thermal energy networks to see if Rhode Island can meet its goals by using this technology. It also sets up a task force of interested groups to advise on the issue. The measure took effect without the governor’s signature.
RI-2026-SB3080.src: Rhode Island legislature, summary (via Open States)

RI-2026-SB3115.s: The bill raises the threshold for calling a vehicle a total loss from 80% to 85%. It affects auto insurance claims for vehicle damage.
RI-2026-SB3115.src: Rhode Island legislature, summary (via Open States)

RI-2026-SB3155.s: The bill exempts the property of the nonprofit Mount St. Rita Health Centre in Cumberland, Rhode Island, from property tax. The tax break would take effect on December 31, 2025.
RI-2026-SB3155.src: Rhode Island legislature, summary (via Open States)

RI-2026-SB3185.s: The bill would make the lake bed and Wilson’s Reservoir in Burrillville exempt from property taxes. It became effective without the governor’s signature.
RI-2026-SB3185.src: Rhode Island legislature, summary (via Open States)

RI-2026-SB3212.s: The act would make changes to state business law to address identity theft aimed at businesses, misleading ads sent to businesses, and the unauthorized creation of business entities. It would add new rules to help stop these acts and deal with them if they happen. The measure was signed by the governor.
RI-2026-SB3212.src: Rhode Island legislature, summary (via Open States)

RI-2026-SB3242.s: This act lets the Chariho Regional School District borrow up to $116 million to build, furnish, and equip a new elementary school. It also covers land purchase, demolition, design, health and safety work, playgrounds, landscaping, paving, and related costs at the Switch Road campus. The school would serve Charlestown, Richmond, and Hopkinton, and state housing aid would have to be approved at a set share of at least 61% when the money is issued.
RI-2026-SB3242.src: Rhode Island legislature, summary (via Open States)

RI-2026-SB3243.s: The bill lets the Town of Portsmouth issue up to $41 million in bonds and notes, which are forms of borrowed money. The money would pay for building work, repairs, updates, and equipment for schools and other school facilities across the town.
RI-2026-SB3243.src: Rhode Island legislature, summary (via Open States)

RI-2026-SB3262.s: The law changes the property tax exemption rules for elderly and disabled people in the town of Glocester. It affects homeowners there who may qualify for that tax break. It became law without the governor's signature.
RI-2026-SB3262.src: Rhode Island legislature, summary (via Open States)

RI-2026-SB3315.s: The law lets the town of Coventry split its local tax levy between homes and businesses in proportion to each type of property. It passed the legislature and became law without the governor’s signature on June 26, 2026.
RI-2026-SB3315.src: Rhode Island legislature, summary (via Open States)

RI-2026-SB3316.s: The bill would require advance notice and posting of motions made from the floor at Scituate’s annual financial town meeting. It affects the town of Scituate and the people who take part in that meeting.
RI-2026-SB3316.src: Rhode Island legislature, summary (via Open States)

RI-2026-SB3321.s: The act lets Pawtucket issue up to $2 million in bonds or notes to renovate, build, rebuild, and equip public recreation facilities, including buying land. The money can also cover related project costs, temporary notes, and the cost of issuing the debt. It was passed by the legislature and signed by the governor.

RI-2026-SB3333.s: The bill changes the law for the North Tiverton fire district and lowers the number of tax assessors from six to four after the annual 2026 meeting, after any voluntary resignations. It became law on June 26, 2026, without the governor's signature.
RI-2026-SB3333.src: Rhode Island legislature, summary (via Open States)

RI-2026-SB3335.s: Warwick would get authority to sell the property at 34 Warwick Lake Avenue without following one state limit, so the city can clear the title to that property. The bill passed and became effective without the governor's signature on June 26, 2026.
RI-2026-SB3335.src: Rhode Island legislature, summary (via Open States)

RI-2026-SB3355.s: The measure lets the city of Cranston issue up to $25 million in bonds and notes to help pay for school land and buildings. The money can be used to buy property and to build, fix, improve, furnish, and equip school facilities across the city. It became effective without the governor's signature.
RI-2026-SB3355.src: Rhode Island legislature, summary (via Open States)

RI-2026-SB3356.s: Allows the city of Cranston to borrow up to $4 million by issuing general obligation bonds and temporary notes. The money would pay for playgrounds, athletic fields, and related equipment, including buying, building, improving, fixing, and changing them. It became effective without the governor's signature on June 26, 2026.
RI-2026-SB3356.src: Rhode Island legislature, summary (via Open States)

RI-2026-SB3358.s: The measure lets Cranston borrow up to $8 million by selling bonds and short-term notes. The money would pay for fire and public safety equipment, including buying, fixing, and updating it. It passed and became effective without the governor’s signature.
RI-2026-SB3358.src: Rhode Island legislature, summary (via Open States)

RI-2026-SB3359.s: The act lets the City of Cranston issue up to $8 million in general obligation bonds and notes to pay for street, sidewalk, and bridge work, including paving, drainage, traffic control devices, road equipment, safety fixes, and landscaping. It also lets the city use the money for related bond costs, temporary notes, and capitalized interest. The law took effect on June 26, 2026, and it affects Cranston and its taxpayers, since the city must repay the debt through property taxes if needed.

RI-2026-SB3361.s: The bill would let foreclosure notices and notices about active-duty military rights be sent by regular first-class mail or by an overnight delivery service. It affects people involved in mortgage foreclosures and active military service members.
RI-2026-SB3361.src: Rhode Island legislature, summary (via Open States)

RI-2026-SB3362.s: The bill would let the state motor vehicle office offer special vehicle registration plates for the Dominican Independence and Heritage Award Committee of Rhode Island, a nonprofit group. These plates would be available to people who want them through the normal vehicle registration process.
RI-2026-SB3362.src: Rhode Island legislature, summary (via Open States)

RI-2026-SB3363.s: The law lets the town of Tiverton set up, by local rule, a real estate tax credit for seniors age 65 and older. It affects older homeowners in Tiverton and took effect without the governor's signature.
RI-2026-SB3363.src: Rhode Island legislature, summary (via Open States)

RI-2026-SB3366.s: Creates special motor vehicle registration plates for vehicles linked to the Rhode Island Fire Chiefs Honor Flight Hub, a not-for-profit group. It affects vehicle owners who want these special plates. The bill was signed by the Governor.
RI-2026-SB3366.src: Rhode Island legislature, summary (via Open States)

RI-2026-SB3370.s: The bill exempts Amos House’s real estate and personal property from taxes, as long as it stays a tax-exempt nonprofit under federal law. It applies to Amos House and its taxable property in Rhode Island.
RI-2026-SB3370.src: Rhode Island legislature, summary (via Open States)

RI-2026-SR3353.s: This joint resolution would set aside state money to pay certain claims. It affects the people or groups whose claims are covered by the payment. It became effective without the governor’s signature.
RI-2026-SR3353.src: Rhode Island legislature, summary (via Open States)
